# hitl-mcp-cli

> Human-in-the-Loop MCP Server — lets AI agents pause and request human confirmation, input, or a decision before proceeding with sensitive or ambiguous actions.

## What it does

hitl-mcp-cli is an MCP server that bridges AI autonomy and human judgment. When an AI agent encounters a decision point that requires human input — ambiguous requirements, destructive operations, multi-option choices — it calls one of the HITL tools. The server surfaces the request in a terminal UI (TUI) and blocks until the human responds.

Key capabilities:
- Collect free-form text, file paths, or multiline input from a human
- Present multiple-choice options (single or multi-select, with fuzzy search)
- Gate destructive or sensitive operations behind a yes/no confirmation
- Send non-blocking notifications (success, warning, error, info)
- Log all interactions to `~/.local/state/hitl-mcp/interactions.jsonl`
- Group requests by agent name and project ID in a sessions panel
- Show step progress indicators (Step X/Y) in the TUI header

## Transport

The server runs over **streamable-http** on `http://127.0.0.1:5555/mcp` by default. It requires `"timeout": 0` in the MCP client config because human response time is unbounded.

## MCP Surface (v1.0)

### Tools (agent-callable, blocking)

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `hitl_collect` | Collect a single text, path, or multiline value |
| `hitl_ask` | Alias for `hitl_collect` |
| `hitl_choose` | Present a list of options; returns the selected value(s) |
| `hitl_confirm` | Yes/no gate; supports severity levels and optional timeout |
| `hitl_notify` | Non-blocking notification (success/info/warning/error) |

### Resources (readable state snapshots)

| URI | Content |
|-----|---------|
| `queue://pending` | Interactions currently awaiting human response |
| `queue://history` | Full interaction history for the session |
| `session://activity` | Per-agent/project activity summary |
| `session://last-user-action-age` | Seconds since the last human response |

### Prompts (reusable templates, user-invoked)

| Name | Use case |
|------|---------|
| `hitl_architectural_fork` | Architecture decision with multiple approaches |
| `hitl_destructive_action` | Confirmation template for destructive operations |
| `hitl_scope_clarification` | Clarify ambiguous requirements |
| `hitl_panel_vote_summary` | Multi-option vote with rationale |

## Installation

```bash
# Run without installing
uvx hitl-mcp-cli

# Install globally
uv tool install hitl-mcp-cli
```

## MCP client configuration

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hitl": {
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:5555/mcp",
      "transport": "streamable-http",
      "timeout": 0
    }
  }
}
```

## Usage examples

### Claude Desktop / Claude Code

Add the config above to `claude_desktop_config.json` or `.mcp.json`. The tools appear automatically. Call them from system prompt or tool use:

```
Before deleting files, call hitl_confirm with severity="high".
Before starting a multi-step workflow, call hitl_collect to confirm the target directory.
```

### Kiro / Amazon Q Developer

Same streamable-http config. Add to `.kiro/settings/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hitl": {
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:5555/mcp",
      "transport": "streamable-http",
      "timeout": 0
    }
  }
}
```

### Codex / OpenAI agents

Use the MCP client SDK with the streamable-http transport. Point to `http://127.0.0.1:5555/mcp` and set request timeout to 0 (or the maximum your client supports).

### Cursor / Cline / Windsurf

Add to your MCP settings file under `mcpServers` with the same config block above.

## Tool call examples

```python
# Collect input
name = await hitl_collect(
    message="What should we name this project?",
    default="my-project",
    validation_pattern=r"^[a-z0-9-]+$"
)

# Choose from options
env = await hitl_choose(
    message="Deploy to which environment?",
    choices=["Development", "Staging", "Production"],
    default="Staging"
)

# Confirm a destructive action
result = await hitl_confirm(
    message="Delete 150 deprecated files?",
    severity="high",
    context="This cannot be undone."
)
if result["action"] == "accept":
    delete_files()

# Non-blocking notification
await hitl_notify(
    message="Deployment complete",
    level="success",
    title="Done"
)
```

## Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `HITL_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | Server bind address |
| `HITL_PORT` | `5555` | Server port |
| `HITL_LOG_LEVEL` | `ERROR` | Log verbosity (DEBUG/INFO/WARNING/ERROR) |
| `HITL_NO_BANNER` | `false` | Suppress startup banner |
